newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen higher after CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen higher after CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Thursday following a report on July inflation at the retail level that matched expectations, analysts said. The following are their comments:
ROY BLUMBERG, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST JOSEPHTHAL LYON & ROSS: "It's basically painless to the economy....the stock market should be firm at the opening at this point."
The government reported the July Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent overall and rose 0.2 percent at the core rate, which excludes the volatile food and energy components.
Economists in a Reuters poll had expected, on average, for the CPI to be up 0.2 percent overall and up 0.2 percent at the core rate.

Blumberg added that the data would be "interpreted as a moderate positive to the bond market (but) the bond market is being affected as much by the dollar as by economic data at this point. So barring any major catastrophes to the dollar today, it's modestly bullish for the bond market and should be bullish for the stock market."

SHERRY COOPER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, NESBITT BURNS: "The number is just as expected -- it's good news for the markets. At least we didn't get a nasty shock, and on the heels of yesterday's PPI decline, this should cause the markets to breathe a sigh of relief."

HARRY LAUBSCHER, MARKET ANALYST WITH TUCKER ANTHONY: "I would expect the market to attempt to continue the rally started later yesterday, but the stocks are not going to run away and there will be selling into strength."
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32 to yield 6.59 percent, down from Wednesday's close at 6.63 percent.
The S&P 500 future was up 5.00 to 930.80.
